skill.name: execution-engine-analysis

The text asks the assistant to identify async and topology models in a target codebase, which matches the skill purpose. It does not request host reconnaissance, credential discovery, or system enumeration.
This location is a subsection title for the hybrid concurrency classification. It does not instruct the assistant to enumerate the host system or collect sensitive environment details.

content.value_statement: Agent frameworks hide concurrency, topology, events, and hooks across many files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured execution-engine review.
actual_capabilities: Classifies execution models as native async, sync-with-wrappers, or hybrid.
Identifies topology patterns such as DAG, finite state machine, or linear chain.
Catalogs callbacks, event listeners, emitters, and streaming generators.
Maps observability hook points before and after LLM, tool, step, and error handling.
Produces a markdown report covering concurrency, topology, events, hooks, and scalability.
limitations: Requires source files or repository context to inspect execution behavior.
Does not run benchmarks or measure live performance.
Does not replace a full security review of framework execution.
May miss dynamic behavior hidden behind reflection, plugins, or generated code.

use_cases.title: Review a New Agent Framework
use_cases.description: Map how a framework schedules work, handles async calls, and exposes hooks before adoption.

use_cases.title: Document Runtime Architecture
use_cases.description: Create a consistent execution report for maintainers, contributors, and technical documentation.

use_cases.title: Compare Scaling Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare concurrency, event flow, and observability across frameworks before platform integration.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze the provided agent framework. Classify its concurrency model, execution topology, event architecture, observability hooks, and scalability limits.

prompt_templates.title: Map Events and Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to catalog all callback, listener, emitter, streaming, and error hooks. Note where hooks can observe, modify, or redirect execution.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Execution Engines
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare these two agent frameworks. Highlight differences in async support, graph or state models, event registration, streaming, and operational scalability.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Scalability Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to assess the execution engine for production scaling. Identify blocking paths, concurrency boundaries, resource limits, backpressure points, and observability gaps.

output_examples.input: Analyze an agent framework that exposes both invoke and async invoke methods.
output_examples.output: The report classifies the framework as hybrid, explains the sync and async entry points, and lists evidence for each path.

output_examples.input: Review a graph-based workflow engine with callbacks and streaming responses.
output_examples.output: The report identifies a DAG topology, catalogs callback and streaming hooks, and summarizes where execution can be observed or modified.

output_examples.input: Compare two frameworks before choosing one for a production agent platform.
output_examples.output: The report contrasts concurrency models, event systems, hook flexibility, and scaling risks in a concise decision matrix.

best_practices: Provide execution entry points and core orchestration files.
Ask for evidence with file and function references for each classification.
Review async behavior, topology, events, hooks, and scalability together.
anti_patterns: Do not classify a framework from README claims alone.
Do not ignore sync wrappers around async internals.
Do not treat every callback system as full observability.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes concurrency models, execution topology, event architecture, observability hooks, and scalability characteristics in agent frameworks.

faq.question: Does it execute my code?
faq.answer: No. It guides static architectural review using files and context you provide.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare execution models, event systems, hook designs, and scalability tradeoffs across frameworks.

faq.question: Does it find performance bugs?
faq.answer: It can identify likely blocking points and scaling risks, but it does not measure runtime performance.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide execution entry points, orchestration files, callback modules, streaming code, and graph or state definitions.
